Modeling early-life stress: long-term behavioral and neurobiological effects. Maternal separation (MS), maternal deprivation (MD), and limited bedding and nesting (LBN) are used as rodent models of early-life stress. This figure shows that stress experienced during the postnatal period (P2–21) can lead to significant and lasting changes in both behavioral and neurobiological outcomes in adulthood.
